item.title: In Conversation: Doug Jones + Hellboy II: The Golden Army | Jorgensen Guest Filmmaker Series — Wed Nov 18, 6:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Join us for a conversation with Doug Jones, one of the most versatile actors working today and the modern successor to classic screen icon Lon Chaney. The program will begin with an onstage conversation with Jones, followed by a screening of Hellboy II: The Golden Army, which features an acclaimed performance by Jones as Abe Sapien. After the film, Jones will return to the stage for a post-film chat and take questions from the audience. Note: your tickets to the conversation also includes viewing the film.
Hellboy II: The Golden Army, Guillermo del Toro's follow-up to his smash comic book adaptation, once again finds our (anti) hero, his pyrokinetic girlfriend, and aquatic empath (Doug Jones) facing their biggest battle when an underworld prince plans to reclaim Earth for his magical kindred. Only Hellboy and company can stop the dark prince and prevent humanity's annihilation. [120 min; action, fantasy; English]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Nov 19 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Nov 19 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Nov 19 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Health Economics Webinar — Thu Nov 19, 7:00 AM
item.description: Health economic evaluations are vital for identifying high-impact, cost-effective interventions and guiding the efficient allocation of limited healthcare resources. The AMPATH Kenya partnership has long demonstrated the value of integrated clinical care, education, research, and health system strengthening to improve health outcomes across Kenya and beyond. As AMPATH continues to expand its research portfolio and translate evidence into policy and practice, understanding the economic dimensions of health has become increasingly essential to ensuring that proven health interventions are both scalable and sustainable. This special Moi University School of Medicine Grand Rounds session will introduce core health economics concepts and demonstrate how economic principles, methods, and evidence can inform clinical decision-making, research design, program implementation, and health policy. The session also serves as a preview of the new AMPATH Health Economics Core, which will launch in 20

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Thu Nov 19, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Animal Hour / Dive Deeper — Fri Nov 20, 3:00 PM — Wonderlab
item.description:
November Theme: Technology Day: Friday Times 3 - 4pm Recommended for: All ages Event Price Free for Members / Free with Museum Admission Get closer to the wild side with Animal Hour and Dive Deeper! These weekly programs let you chat with WonderLab's animal experts, discover what it takes to care for creatures from around the globe, and meet snakes, lizards, insects, arachnids, and more-up close and out of their habitats. Animal Hour takes place on most Fridays, while Dive Deeper happens on the last Friday of each month at WonderLab's stunning coral reef aquarium. Type of Activities Animal Hour: Meet our animal ambassadors. Observe the tools we use to care for our animal ambassadors. Type of Activities Dive Deeper: Tour the reef system and learn the mechanics behind how it functions.
Source: Limestone Post

item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Wed Nov 25 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Wed Nov 25 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. item.title: Open Studio — Wed Nov 25, 1:00 PM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description:
Our Open Studio program invites participants to create in the museum's art studio, where art becomes a tool for reflection, expression, and connection. Guided by a trained art therapist, the open studio welcomes visitors to engage with materials at their own pace while drawing inspiration from the surrounding exhibitions. No art experience is needed; just bring your curiosity and a desire to create, and we'll handle the rest! Participants are welcome to utilize supplies located in the studio, as well as bring their own supplies/projects to work on. This group meets on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of every month, excluding holidays and museum closures. It is open to everyone: students, staff, and the public included! The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.
Source: Architecture + Design, IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Eskenazi School of Art

item.description:
November Theme: Technology Day: Friday Times 3 - 4pm Recommended for: All ages Event Price Free for Members / Free with Museum Admission Get closer to the wild side with Animal Hour and Dive Deeper! These weekly programs let you chat with WonderLab's animal experts, discover what it takes to care for creatures from around the globe, and meet snakes, lizards, insects, arachnids, and more-up close and out of their habitats. Type of Activities Animal Hour: Meet our animal ambassadors. Observe the tools we use to care for our animal ambassadors. Type of Activities Dive Deeper: Tour the reef system and learn the mechanics behind how it functions.
